images.title: Whole blocks and a part
images.purpose: Show the one idea the student practises: counting equal parts along a number line, every full unit becomes a whole, and the parts past it are the fraction left.
images.composition: One number line across the frame, a solid block over the first unit and a lighter band over the parts after it, with one marked end point.
images.exact_structure: A grey #6B7280 number line from 0 to 2 with exactly 9 evenly spaced ticks: each unit cut into 4 equal parts. A solid teal #0072B2 block covers exactly 0 to 1. An amber #E69F00 band covers exactly the 3 parts from 1 to the 3rd tick after 1, split by thin lines into 3 equal pieces. A reddish purple #CC79A7 point sits at the end of the amber band. Exactly 1 number line, 1 block, 1 band.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
any on-screen control, panel or app frame drawn around the number line
images.takeaway: Each full unit is a whole; the parts past it are the fraction left over.
images.description: A number line from 0 to 2 in fourths; a teal block fills 0 to 1 and an amber band covers 3 more fourths, ending at a purple point labelled 7/4 = 1 3/4.
images.context: Shown with the doer concept before the student practises. PLACEHOLDER: specified, not generated yet.
images.teaching_notes: Ask the student to count all the fourths from 0 to the point, then say the same length as wholes and a part.

image_decisions.why: One picture of a whole block and a leftover band primes the fraction and mixed number practice.
